long_biography.plain_text:
Laurene Powell Jobs earned degrees in political science and economics from the University of Pennsylvania and an MBA from Stanford. After early work in investment banking, she co-founded a natural-foods business and established College Track, a college-access organisation. She later founded Emerson Collective, combining investment, philanthropy and advocacy across education, immigration, health, climate and economic opportunity.

Her principal fortune did not arise from those ventures. She inherited holdings in Apple and Walt Disney following the death of her husband, Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, in 2011. Powell Jobs has used that capital through Emerson Collective and related foundations, including investments in media and support for education and environmental programmes. Her enduring public role is therefore dual: beneficiary and steward of inherited technology and media wealth, and independent founder of institutions directing that capital toward social impact.
